subject: Stream handshake and TTFT window — alignment and fallbacks
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@adroithealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@adroithealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Stream handshake and TTFT window — initial alignment and next steps

Hi Marta / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can size the pilot and scope the SLA: I pulled out the perf targets you described and added a small set of clarifying questions.

Summary of your targets (please correct):
- Primary TTFT target: median <= 120 ms, p95 <= 300 ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 50 concurrent interactive users (~175 reqs/min peak, estimate ~12k tokens/min)
- Streaming behavior: prefer SSE for server -> client in initial rollout; may require WebSocket if we need multiplexed tool calls or lower-level acks later.
- Chunk cadence: you want first chunk immediately (0–40 ms added) then subsequent chunks at ~150–250 ms cadence depending on tokenization.

Questions we promised to clarify:
1) Do you consider the TTFT window to include initial network handshake (TLS + proxy) on your side, or should we budget a 30–50 ms client-network buffer?
2) For large multimodal prompts (attachments + context), what fraction of requests do you expect to be short (<=128 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens)? A sample distribution will help our kernel selection and warmstart strategy.
3) Any strict proxies or corporate NGFW that would block long-lived SSEs? If so, we should design a WS fallback.

Proposed pilot plan (what Redwood will deliver):
- 48-hour pilot on a dedicated test pool (same GPU class we plan for production) with real sample payloads.
- Instrumented telemetry for TTFT (server-side emit time), first-byte RTT, p50/p95/p99; chunk cadence and chunk size distribution.
- Two fallback modes: SSE primary; WebSocket fallback (client negotiates via HTTP header) if SSE fails.
- Sample SLA draft attached (Adroit_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) with TTFT windows we discussed.

Next steps we agreed on today:
- Marta / Samir: share 48 hours of representative payloads + proxy notes and the sample traffic distribution (short/medium/long) by EOD Monday.
- Redwood: send pilot config and sample chunk profile template (attached: sample_chunk_profile.csv) by tomorrow.
- Quick kickoff call to schedule the 48-hour run once payloads are in (I suggested Tue/Wed window).

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the pilot config + required client test harness.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 17:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Stream handshake and TTFT window — initial alignment and next steps

Neha —

This looks right, thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- TTFT window: we want the SLO to apply to the server-side emit time (i.e., time from request received at Redwood to first token emitted). Our front-end has a consistent 20–40 ms proxy layer; please include a 30 ms buffer in your planning.
- Request distribution: roughly 65% short (<=128), 25% medium (129–512), 10% long (>512). I attached a short CSV export you can use.
- Proxies: two enterprise customers in our pilot use a corporate NGFW that drops long-poll connections after 5 minutes; SSE for typical responses is fine. For long-running streams (>5 min) we’ll need WS fallback — not a blocker for initial pilot.

Two asks from us:
1) Can Redwood instrument and include a breakdown of network vs server-side latency in the pilot report? That will help our SREs tune client-side timeouts.
2) If the pilot shows p95 TTFT > 300 ms, what are typical mitigation levers (more GPUs, different kernel, quantization change, prefix caching)? We want to understand tradeoffs ahead of the SLA.

Happy to share the payload CSV now — attaching. We can kick off as soon as you confirm the start window.

— Marta
Marta Lopez, Head of Platform Engineering
AdroitHealth
[attachment: adh_sample_distribution.csv (csv)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marta Lopez <marta@adroithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stream handshake and TTFT window — initial alignment and next steps

Quick technical note based on Marta’s distribution and their TTFT targets:

- Baseline sizing: with 65% short requests and target median 120 ms server-side TTFT, we should be able to meet goals on our T4-class test nodes with a warm KV cache and continuous batching tuned to 8–12 in-flight requests. If they want tighter p95 (~200–250 ms), we’ll recommend a dedicated V100/RTX-like class or opt into lower-precision kernels (4-bit quant) for dense models.
- Chunk cadence: their requested 150–250 ms cadence is realistic if we emit ~32-token chunks and avoid too-small chunk sizes (which increase overhead). I recommend an initial cadence config: first chunk immediate (emitted as soon as logits available), then 200 ms target spacing with adaptive pacing when GPU is saturated.
- Handshake/window budgeting: honor the 30 ms client buffer Marta cited. On top of that, we’ll set an internal headroom of ~40 ms to cover TLS handshake when possible (we’ll baseline during the pilot).
- Fallbacks: implement SSE primary + WS fallback. For NGFWs that kill long lived sessions we’ll include short keepalive heartbeats (every 90s) and an HTTP polling fallback for extreme networks (last resort).

Action items for Redwood engineering (I’ll take lead):
- Prepare pilot config (pool size, GPU class options, batching params, quant profile) and a short runbook for how we’ll measure server-side TTFT and separate out network time.
- Add a metric in the pilot dashboard: first_token_server_emit_ms, first_byte_client_rtt_ms, chunk_interarrival_ms distribution.

I’ll drop a config doc to the Drive link Neha shared and sync with Ben on telemetry dashboards.

— Karthik
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marta / Karthik — this is great. Confirming final pilot plan & schedule:

- Start window: Tue 11 May 2027 09:00 PT — 48 hours
- Test pool: 2 x V100-equivalent nodes (initial); we’ll scale to 4 if p95 > 300 ms during the pilot
- Traffic: use the attached distribution + 30% synthetic jitter to model burstiness
- Measurement: Redwood will provide a pilot report with server-side TTFT (p50/p95/p99), client-observed first-byte, and chunk cadence histogram. We’ll surface a recommended mitigation plan if p95 exceeds 300 ms (scale up GPUs, increase batching, enable 4-bit kernels, enable prefix caching).
- Doc/links: HubSpot deal linked; Drive folder active (I uploaded the pilot config). I’ll also route a DocuSign link for the pilot terms if Adroit wants a quick one-off pilot agreement.

Next steps for Adroit:
- Please confirm the Tue start and drop the payloads + any proxy configs to the Drive folder by Mon EOD (we need the proxy header behavior to test SSE fallback).
- If you want a WS-only run for a subset of traffic, tell us which fraction (we can split 20/80).

I’ll send the kickoff invite once Marta confirms. Thanks everyone — excited to get this live.

-neha
